_comment: The week in the DFFL. The scheduled job appends one object to weeks[] after each week finalizes: a lede, a write-up for each of the six games, and an 'around' notebook covering everything else that moved that week. articles[] holds longer pieces — draft reports, midseason takes — which are written by hand or on request rather than by the weekly job; the job must carry articles[] through untouched. The site sorts both newest-first and computes risers and sliders itself from its own power rankings, so nothing here should ever quote a rank or a movement.

weeks[].lede: one paragraph on the week as a whole - the shape of it, what mattered, what it set up

around[].kind: one of: trade, waivers, riser, slider, streak, injury, race, note
around[].headline: short, factual

articles[].headline: the piece's title
articles[].standfirst: optional short detail line next to the byline

blocks[].p: {type:'p', text, lead?}  - a paragraph; lead:true gets the drop cap. <b> is allowed, nothing else
blocks[].bars: {type:'bars', title, sub, rows:[{label, sub, value, group}]}  - diverging bars about zero; group 1-3 picks the colour
blocks[].cards: {type:'cards', items:[{title, big, sub, lead?, rows:[{label, value}]}]}

weeks.lede: Six games and 1401.7 points between them, 235.6 fewer than the opening week, and the week was the better for it. jadencha put up 145.1 and beat moseslin by 66.8, the only blowout on the slate; four of the other five were settled by fewer than 28. bertalicious and saucebossandrew needed 251.94 between them to separate by 11.62. Domo112 went from the second-best score in the league to 85.32 and lost by 27.32. Three teams are 2-0, three are 0-2, and the six in between are all 1-1 — and the points-for table does not agree with any of it.

games.headline: bertalicious holds on in the closest game of the week
games.body: The tightest game of the week and the highest-scoring — 251.94 between them, settled by 11.62. Ja'Marr Chase went for 26.5 and Stefon Diggs 21.7, and Baker Mayfield returned 13.18 in his first week on the roster after bertalicious dropped Jared Goff for him. saucebossandrew's 120.16 was the best losing score of week 2, with 44.5 more sitting on his bench.

games.headline: Allen and Adams both clear 40; bradyrife has more behind his
games.body: Josh Allen's 40.82 and Davante Adams's 40.5 were the second- and third-best individual scores of the week, on opposite sides of the same game. The difference was everything else: Christian McCaffrey added 20.6 and George Kittle 19 for bradyrife, while nobody in the jskule23 lineup besides Allen cleared 14. jskule23 left 10.1 on his bench, the least of any manager in the league — this was the team he had.

games.headline: wesley55's defence outscores most of a lineup
games.body: Carolina's 27 was the best score in the wesley55 lineup, a week after he added the unit and dropped Pittsburgh for it. Jaylen Waddle (22.8) and James Cook (21.4) did the rest. chassinator got 20.3 out of Jake Ferguson, himself a free-agent pickup that week, but started Rhamondre Stevenson for 3.1 and left 55.2 on the bench, Tre Tucker's 25.9 included.

games.headline: victorthompson makes seven moves and wins by 18
games.body: Seven roster moves in a week, and the two that mattered both started: Dak Prescott for 29.76 and Devaughn Vele, claimed for $6, for 11.4. New England's 23 was the second-best defensive score anywhere on the slate. sizzlemc2 lost this one in his tight end slot, which is its own story.

games.headline: jadencha wins by 66.8 and has not been tested yet
games.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 44.5 was the best individual score of the week and Amon-Ra St. Brown's 35.2 was not far behind; between them they nearly covered the 66.8-point margin on their own. moseslin managed 78.3, the lowest score of week 2, and got 2.5 from Saquon Barkley. jadencha has now won by 70.8 and 66.8 and has scored 341.0, more than any other manager in the league.

games.headline: Domo112 falls 101 points off his own pace
games.body: Domo112 scored 187.06 in the opening week, the second-best score in the league. He followed it with 85.32, a drop of 101.74 and the second-lowest score of week 2, with 1.1 from Malik Nabers and 1.3 from Colston Loveland. drewkim did not need much — DeVonta Smith's 27.7 and Omarion Hampton's 16.5 covered it — and still left 67.88 unused, Brock Purdy's 28.48 among it.

around.headline: Week 3: jadencha and Domo112, 613.38 points between them
around.body: The headline game of week 3 pairs jadencha, 2-0 with 341.0 points, against Domo112 at 1-1 with 272.38 — the most combined scoring of any week 3 pairing. jadencha has won by 70.8 and 66.8 and has not yet played a close game; Domo112 owns both the second-best single week in the league and the steepest fall of week 2. The next-heaviest pairing is wesley55 and sizzlemc2 at 523.68.

around.headline: Three unbeaten, three winless, and a points table that disagrees
around.body: jadencha, wesley55 and bradyrife are 2-0; chassinator, moseslin and jskule23 are 0-2. Scoring does not explain the split: sizzlemc2 is 1-1 on 273.64, more than either unbeaten team other than jadencha, and moseslin is 0-2 on 240.16, which is more than bradyrife has scored while winning twice. Six of the twelve make the playoffs and 72 games remain.

around.headline: bertalicious and victorthompson found forty points; Domo112 lost a hundred
around.body: The two lowest scores of the opening week were bertalicious's 90.74 and victorthompson's 90.5. Both won in week 2, on 131.78 and 129.26 — swings of 41.04 and 38.76, the largest in the league in either direction bar one. That one is Domo112, down 101.74 from 187.06 to 85.32, with moseslin next at 83.56 lower.

around.headline: victorthompson dropped Patrick Mahomes for a $6 receiver
around.body: Seven moves, and the one that will be remembered is releasing Patrick Mahomes to claim Devaughn Vele for $6. Vele started and returned 11.4, while Dak Prescott — already on the roster — went for 29.76. jskule23 dropped Vele in the same waiver run and spent $1 on Makai Lemon, who did not start. Eight dollars changed hands across the whole league.

around.headline: Eight trades in week 1, none in week 2
around.body: The market that moved Christian McCaffrey twice in the opening week produced nothing at all in the second. Every roster change in week 2 came off waivers or the free-agent pool, and only three of the twenty-two cost a dollar. bradyrife has still committed more budget than anyone this season at $36.

around.headline: Four rosters are carrying a man who will not play again this month
around.body: Zach Charbonnet is on the physically-unable-to-perform list after ACL surgery and is not expected back before 11 October. Jordan Mason (thumb, surgery) is dated to 25 October, Omar Cooper (ankle) to 18 October, and De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle, surgery) to 22 November. All four are on DFFL rosters, and none of them counts against a lineup that leaves him out.

weeks.lede: Six games, and the scoreboard split almost exactly down the middle of the league: the three highest-scoring teams all won, and so did the three lowest. jadencha opened with 195.9 and buried drewkim by more than seventy. Domo112 and moseslin combined for 348.92 in the best game of the day and moseslin still went home with nothing. At the other end, bradyrife and bertalicious needed only 195.94 between them to settle a game, which is less than jadencha managed on his own.

games.headline: Domo112 survives the shootout
games.body: The highest-scoring game of the week by some distance — 348.92 between them, and neither side ever really stopped. Caleb Williams put up 37.26 for Domo112, the best single performance anywhere on the slate. moseslin's 161.86 would have beaten three of the six winning scores; it did not beat this one. Domo112 got there despite a starting tight end who finished on nothing.

games.headline: jadencha opens with 195.9
games.body: The week's high score and its widest margin, 70.8 points, and it was never close. D'Andre Swift led with 32.9 in a lineup where the scoring was spread rather than stacked. jadencha also left 54 points on his bench, which is the sort of detail that only reads as a problem in a week you lose. drewkim's 125.1 was not a disaster; it simply arrived on the wrong Sunday.

games.headline: sizzlemc2 holds off chassinator
games.body: Kenneth Walker's 35.6 gave sizzlemc2 the cushion and chassinator never quite closed the 18.14 that separated them. Ashton Jeanty answered with 30.7 but got thin support — Terry McLaurin managed 3.4. Both benches were loud, 50.6 and 44.9 unused respectively, in a game decided by less than either.

games.headline: saucebossandrew edges the closest game
games.body: Twelve and three-quarter points, the tightest result of the week. Josh Allen's 35.66 was the best number on the field and it belonged to the losing side; jskule23 got almost nothing behind him and watched another 43.6 sit on his bench. Chris Olave's 30.2 was enough for saucebossandrew, who did not need a second big score and did not get one.

games.headline: wesley55 wins the low-scoring half
games.body: Derrick Henry's 35.8 accounted for nearly a third of wesley55's total, which tells you how quiet the rest of it was — Kyle Pitts finished on zero and it did not matter. victorthompson's 90.5 was the week's lowest score, with Ladd McConkey's 19.2 the only real contribution and 35.36 stranded on the bench.

games.headline: bradyrife takes the quietest game of the week
games.body: 195.94 combined, the lowest-scoring game on the slate, settled by 14.46. Trevor Lawrence's 26.1 was as good as it got for bradyrife. bertalicious lost while leaving 53.64 on his bench — more than half his starting total again, and comfortably more than the margin.

around.headline: Eight trades, and McCaffrey moved twice
around.body: Christian McCaffrey went from chassinator to bradyrife in a swap that sent Kyren Williams the other way with a pair of picks, then turned up on chassinator's roster again in a separate deal with Domo112 that cost Jahmyr Gibbs. chassinator was involved in three of the eight trades on record, which is a lot of activity for a manager who then lost his opener.

around.headline: jskule23 pays a pick for Luther Burden
around.body: A straight player-for-pick with wesley55 — Burden across, an eighth-rounder back. jskule23 also swapped first-round picks with bertalicious in a separate deal. Both of them lost in week 1.

around.headline: Nobody spent a dollar
around.body: Forty-nine free-agent moves went through and not one of them cost FAAB. Every manager still has his full budget, which will not last, but it does mean the first genuine waiver war is still ahead.

around.headline: The benches were the story
around.body: bertalicious left 53.64 unused and lost by 14.46. jskule23 left 43.6 and lost by 12.76. chassinator left 44.9 and lost by 18.14. All three would have won the game they played with a lineup they already owned.

around.headline: Two starters finished on zero, and both teams won anyway
around.body: Kyle Pitts for wesley55 and Colston Loveland for Domo112 both posted nothing. Neither cost their manager the week, which says more about the opposition than the tight ends.

articles.headline: Bradyrife Bought the Backup Too
articles.dek: Christian McCaffrey arrived by trade last week. Kaelon Black just arrived by the highest FAAB bid of the round — same 49ers backfield, same fantasy roster.

blocks.text: The waiver wire that had not processed as of Monday has now cleared, and the two managers who spent real money went and built things. wesley55 paid $21 for Romeo Doubs. bradyrife paid $36 for Kaelon Black — the highest bid to clear this round — and in doing so added the backup running back to a backfield he already controls the starter of.
What bradyrife paid for Kaelon Black, San Francisco's backup running back. It is the highest FAAB bid to clear this waiver round, and $15 more than the next one.
One Manager, Two 49ers

bradyrife already owns Christian McCaffrey, acquired last week in a trade with chassinator that also sent Kyren Williams the other way. McCaffrey scored 11.3 in his bradyrife debut. Black has not played a snap for the roster yet, but the price says this was insurance rather than a speculative stash — bradyrife spent more on the backup than anyone else spent on anything this round.
The corresponding drop was easy. bradyrife let go of Ja'Kobi Lane, a wide receiver who has been on injured reserve.
Five managers spent nothing at all. Domo112, sizzlemc2, saucebossandrew, moseslin and victorthompson carried their full FAAB budget into week 2 untouched.

articles.headline: The CPES Problem
articles.dek: The two best rosters in the league landed in the same division. One of them is going to spend the autumn fighting for a wildcard — and that is only the second-most interesting thing about this draft.

blocks.text: Corrected 18 August 2026, twice. This piece first ran with market prices from a standard-scoring draft board; DFFL is not standard — a catch is worth a full point to receivers and tight ends and half a point to backs — so every market comparison has been recomputed against the PPR board and the projections with it. It also ran with a keeper list the site had guessed at, because Sleeper records this league's keepers on only two picks. The real list is now written down and the piece is built on it. Two sections changed outright.

The draft is in. Fifteen rounds, a hundred and eighty picks, and a board that looks nothing like the standings it came from. The team with the worst record in the league drafted like it had a plan. The team that won eleven games drafted like it was already satisfied. And a running back the market values inside the top twenty-five sat on the board until the fourteenth round.
What follows is the shape of it: who won the night, who has a problem they cannot see yet, and which division just became the hardest place in the league to survive.

blocks.title: Where the model has everybody
blocks.sub: Projected points per week, shown as distance from the league average of 129.4. Colour is division.

blocks.text: jadencha finally has the roster to match the record

He has been the best regular-season manager in this league since it started — 38-18, a 68 percent win rate, comfortably the highest of the twelve — and he has never won it. Four seasons, four different champions, and none of them him.

This draft did not fix that. It did make it much harder to explain away. His keeper set alone is absurd: Jonathan Taylor in the first round, Amon-Ra St. Brown in the sixth, Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the eighth. Two players the market drafts inside the top ten overall, acquired at picks 71 and 89. Nobody else in the league carried anything close.
jadencha's title odds — well clear of the defending champion's 20 percent, and more than the bottom six teams hold between them.

The model has him at 143.2 points a week, three and a half clear of the field, with a 90 percent chance of making the playoffs. The counter-argument is the only one that has ever mattered here: he has been the best team before.
CPES is where the season gets decided

Here is the structural problem. The two best rosters in the league — jadencha and the defending champion Domo112 — are in the same four-team division. Only one of them can win it. The other has to come through the wildcard places, which are the three best records left over from everybody else.

items.title: CPES
items.sub: Average projection — 4.7 points a week clear of the next division

items.title: Pool 2
items.sub: Top-heavy — one clear favourite and three teams sharing the rest

items.title: Pool 3
items.sub: The softest route to a top-three seed, and nobody in it is above 37 percent

blocks.text: Read those three columns next to each other and the unfairness is obvious. The whole of Pool 3 projects below the league average, and one of those four teams is guaranteed a top-three seed and a shot at a bye. In CPES, the second-best roster in the entire league is a 36 percent shot to win its own division.
Domo112 will probably be fine — 83 percent to make the playoffs is not a crisis. But the bye matters here, and the path to one runs through a team the model likes more.
Nobody in this league drafts quarterbacks

One starting quarterback slot, fifteen rounds, and a room that has clearly done the maths. Four of the five biggest falls in the entire open draft were quarterbacks, and a fifth quarterback was kept in the fifteenth round rather than risk him reaching the room at all:

Every one of those fell past where the wider market takes them, and the money went somewhere specific instead: young running backs, aggressively. Every one of the six biggest reaches in the draft was a running back: Brian Robinson 64 picks early to moseslin, Blake Corum 58 early to the same manager, Woody Marks 58 early to victorthompson, Jacory Croskey-Merritt 54 early to Domo112, Tyrone Tracy 52 early to wesley55, Tyler Allgeier 50 early to bertalicious. Not one reach in the top six was a receiver.

It is a coherent league-wide read — one quarterback slot makes the position replaceable, two running back slots plus two flex spots makes backs scarce, and a receiver's point per catch is already priced into where the market takes him. It is also the kind of consensus that gets a whole room beaten by the one manager who zags.
Puka Nacua cost a fifteenth-round pick

Thirty-six players were kept across the twelve teams, and the gap between what they are worth and what they cost is the whole shape of this league. jskule23 kept Puka Nacua — the third player off the board in the wider market — with the 179th pick. bertalicious kept Bucky Irving at 175. moseslin kept Nico Collins at 149. saucebossandrew kept De'Von Achane, a top-ten back, in the ninth round.

picks between Puka Nacua's market price and the one jskule23 actually paid — the largest keeper discount in the league. The biggest fall in the open draft was also a quarterback: Brock Purdy, 71 picks.

At the other end, three managers kept a player at more or less exactly what he costs anybody: moseslin paid pick 20 for Saquon Barkley, whose market price is 20. jadencha paid pick 8 for Jonathan Taylor, market price 8. bradyrife paid 10 for Christian McCaffrey, market 6 — and then kept a fourth, Trevor Lawrence, with the 178th pick against a market price of 92. Those are not bargains, they are declarations — a first-round slot spent to keep a first-round player, which is what a keeper league does to you when your best asset is also your most expensive one.

And one keeper changed hands before it was even kept. Kyren Williams finished last season on bradyrife's roster, was traded to chassinator in the weeks before the draft, and chassinator kept him at pick 167 — a top-35 back for a fourteenth-round slot. That is the market working exactly as designed: bradyrife already had three he liked more, so the fourth became somebody else's bargain.
Three teams the standings are lying about

wesley55 went 4-10 and finished eighth. He now projects fifth in the league and 37 percent to win Pool 3, the best odds in it. The keeper set is why: James Cook in the fourth round, Quinshon Judkins in the fifth, Joe Burrow in the eighth. He is a 54 percent playoff team in the league's weakest division, which is a very different sentence from the one his record writes.

chassinator won this league in 2022 and has been rebuilding loudly ever since. The worst record in the league last season and last place in the toilet bowl for the second year running, eighth in the projection now — but a 24 percent division shot, and a roster he has been assembling in public: a first-round back, a tenth-round quarterback and a fourteenth-round Kyren Williams.

bradyrife is the one nobody will pick, and the numbers are less rude than the reputation. He finished last in 2025 with the worst all-time record in the league at 19-37. His 2026 draft came out fractionally on the right side of average for the first time, which for him is a step forward of some size. He is also the only manager carrying four keepers, and they are 43 percent of his roster's value — the highest share in the league. Chase Brown in the ninth round and Garrett Wilson in the tenth are the kind of holdings that turn a floor into a middle.
Two teams whose draft did not match their season

saucebossandrew had the best record in the league last year at 11-3 — and finished fourth, which tells you the record was already running ahead of the team. He came out of this draft below average on roster value — the fourth-worst draft contribution in the league — and the model has him fourth at 51 percent to make the playoffs. A champion in 2024, so the pedigree is real; the roster is now merely fine.

victorthompson is the sharper warning. He played in last season's final. He projects eleventh. A.J. Brown, Drake London and Ladd McConkey is a genuinely strong set of holdings, but the open draft went badly — Woody Marks 58 picks early, two quarterbacks spent in a league that treats the position as free — and he finishes the night with the third-lowest roster value in the league and a 35 percent playoff chance.
sizzlemc2 belongs in the footnote: fifth last season at 8-6, eleventh in the projection, and the second-largest negative draft contribution in the league at −5.2 points a week.
Somebody has to be twelfth

The model puts drewkim there — last in projected scoring at 123.4, 25 percent to make the playoffs, and the most negative record half of the rating in the league at −3.6. The keeper set is the tell: Jayden Daniels at pick 76 against a market price of 72, Brock Bowers at 72 against 38, Emeka Egbuka in the fifth. One real discount between the three of them, in a league where the top teams are saving a hundred picks apiece. Being in CPES makes it worse: a 3 percent division shot, and two of his three division rivals are the two best teams in the league.

No consolation available, either. The six teams that miss go into a toilet bowl that runs backwards — you advance by losing — and the two worst records enter it a single defeat from the final. chassinator has come last in each of the past two seasons that way. Being bad in this league is not protective; it is the shortest route to the bottom of it.

One thing the projections deliberately do not do is discount a keeper. Puka Nacua is priced at what a top-three player is worth, not at what a fifteenth-round pick usually returns, because he will score like the former whatever he cost. Keepers are between 19 and 43 percent of every roster's value on this board, and that is the single biggest reason the projections disagree with last season's standings.
The caveat, stated plainly

Every projection above comes from the same model the Odds tab runs: each roster valued against the pre-draft PPR market — 6,665 public drafts sampled between 10 and 17 August — and weighted against what each manager has actually scored across four seasons. Draft-day roster value predicts about half of a team's scoring edge. The other half is injuries, waivers, trades and luck, and none of it has happened yet.

It does not know who is hurt. It does not know who is going to be dropped in week three. It has never seen a bye week. Four seasons in, this league has produced four different champions and the best regular-season manager in it has none of them — which is roughly how much a projection in August is worth.

Numbers in this piece were frozen on 18 August 2026, against the PPR market and the keeper list as the league actually set it. The Odds, Power and Race tabs recompute from Sleeper on every load, so they will move; this won't.

articles.headline: I Owe The Toilet Bowl An Apology
articles.dek: I wrote yesterday that this league cannot punish its worst team. I had the bracket upside down. It punishes them better than almost any format I have seen.

blocks.text: This column replaces one published on 19 August 2026 under the headline “Nobody Has Ever Finished Last”. That piece argued that DFFL's consolation bracket protects its worst teams from finishing bottom. It was wrong, top to bottom, for the reason set out below. The original is not preserved; it was wrong on the facts and there is nothing in it worth keeping.

Yesterday I wrote that the two worst teams in this league get byes that make last place unreachable for them, and that the format therefore pays you to give up. I read the bracket, I read the finishing order the site had computed from it, and both agreed with me. Both were wrong, because the thing they were computed from was being read backwards.
You advance by losing

DFFL's consolation bracket is a toilet bowl in the literal sense: the team that loses each tie is the one that goes through. Sleeper records the team that advances in the field marked winner, which is fine for the championship bracket and exactly inverted for this one. Read naively — which is what I did, and what this site did — every result in the bottom bracket comes out the wrong way round.

There is a clean way to check. Compare the bracket's winner against the actual scoreline of the game. Across the four completed seasons the championship bracket agrees with the scores on all twenty-eight ties. The consolation bracket disagrees on all twenty-eight.
consolation ties where the bracket's “winner” is the team that scored fewer points. That is not noise. That is the bracket telling you what it is, in a language I did not read.
The worst two start a game from the bottom

Once you read it the right way up, the design is rather good. The four best teams that missed the playoffs play the first round, and the two that lose keep falling. The two worst records sit that round out — not as a reward, as a head start towards the drop. They enter in the second round already one defeat from the final, and the final is for twelfth.

blocks.title: The 2025 toilet bowl, read correctly
blocks.sub: Winners of each tie escape upward. Losers fall. chassinator and wesley55, the two worst records, enter in round two already one game from the bottom.

blocks.text: chassinator went 3-11, entered in round two, lost to drewkim, lost the final to wesley55 by three points, and finished twelfth. He did not escape anything. He took the whole thing on the chin, which is what I said the format made impossible.
It hits the right team about half the time

Twice out of four the worst record in the league has finished last. The other two times a middling team lost three games in a row at the wrong moment and wore it. That is a competition, not a filing error, and I would rather have it than a table that hands out the punishment automatically in November.

It also produces the single best fact in this league's short history: chassinator won the whole thing in 2022 and has finished last in each of the two seasons since. Champion, then twelfth, then twelfth. No other manager has been to both ends of this league, and he has been to both ends three times in four years.
The data agreed with me, and the data was wrong

The uncomfortable part is that nothing looked broken. The bracket had a winner field and I read it. The site had a finishing order and I quoted it. Both were internally consistent and both were upside down, and a column got published on top of them with a bracket diagram that made the wrong claim look rigorous.

What caught it was somebody who was there saying the result did not match what happened. That is the only check that would have caught it, and it is worth saying plainly: the scoreline is the source of truth here, and everything else on this site is a story told about the scoreline. Where the two disagree, the scoreline wins.

The finishing order for all four seasons has been recomputed and every page that reads it — the records, the trophies, the all-time table, the odds board's price on last place — has moved with it. If you remember finishing eighth in 2023 and the site now says tenth, this is why.

Corrected 19 August 2026. Brackets and finishes are DFFL's own, off the league's Sleeper history, now cross-checked against the weekly scores. Opinions are the writer's; the arithmetic is the league's, and this time it has been checked against the games.

articles.headline: The Nine-Game Difference
articles.dek: Domo112 and saucebossandrew have played five seasons to within a tenth of a win of each other. One of them is 37-19. The other is 28-28.

cover.caption: What the schedule has taken, and given

blocks.text: There is a number this league computes about every manager and almost nobody looks at. It asks a simple question: if you had played all eleven other teams every week instead of the one you were scheduled against, how many would you have beaten? It is the fairest measure of a fantasy team there is, because it throws away the only part of the season nobody controls — who you happened to draw.

Run it over five seasons and it says something uncomfortable. Domo112 has beaten 58.0% of the league week for week. saucebossandrew has beaten 57.8%. They have played, to the nearest tenth of a percentage point, exactly as well as each other.
The difference in earned wins between the two of them across five seasons — 32.45 against 32.36. The difference in actual wins is nine.
Same standard, opposite fortunes

Read those two columns again, because the obvious explanation is not available. Domo112 has not been outscored. He has scored 179 points more than saucebossandrew over five years. He is not the one who has been worse at fantasy football.
Points more that Domo112's opponents have put up against him than saucebossandrew's have. That is the entire story, and he had no say in a single one of them.

Nobody chooses their schedule. Nobody chooses to catch a team in the week its bench explodes. Over fourteen games a year that noise is supposed to wash out, and across five seasons and fifty-six games apiece you would expect it to have washed out by now. It has not. It has compounded in opposite directions until it is worth nine wins.

blocks.title: Wins above and below what the scoring earned
blocks.sub: Actual wins minus the wins each manager's weekly scores deserved, all five seasons

rows.label: jadencha
rows.sub: 38-18, and earned nearly all of it

blocks.text: The best team in the league finished third

The cleanest illustration is a single season. In 2024 Domo112 had the best beat-everyone rate in the league — first of twelve, 66.2%, the most dominant scoring season any DFFL manager has put together. He went 8-6 and finished third. saucebossandrew was fifth by the same measure, 56.5%, went 9-5, and won the championship.

That is not an accusation. saucebossandrew won those playoff games and nobody handed them to him. But the fourteen weeks that decided who got to play them were not measuring what everyone assumed they were measuring.
2025, when it finally broke the other way

Domo112 won the 2025 title. He went 10-4 in a season his beat-everyone rate ranked fifth — his least dominant year of the four in which he has been good. The luck did not correct so much as invert: the manager who had been owed wins for three straight years finally got a schedule that flattered him, and converted it into the only thing that goes on the wall.

There is a version of this league's history where Domo112 has two titles and a reputation, and it is not far away. In 2022 he was the fifth-best scoring team in the league and finished eleventh. He has been quietly excellent for five years and has one banner and a .500 record to show for it.
What to do with this

Nothing, really — that is rather the point. There is no adjustment to make and no lesson to draw about roster construction. The schedule is randomly generated and will keep being randomly generated, and over a long enough run it does not favour anybody.

What it is worth is a small correction to how this league talks about itself. Records are the wrong way to argue about who is good, and they have been misleading everybody for five years about two managers in particular. When somebody is 5-9 and insists they have been unlucky, the honest answer is that they are usually wrong — and that once, here, somebody was right by nine games.

Beat-everyone rate and luck are computed from the full game log on this site: every regular-season score in league history, each week compared against all eleven other scores from that same week. Earned wins are the sum of those weekly win probabilities. Playoffs are excluded throughout — they are a different question. All figures through the end of the 2025 season, before a ball was snapped in 2026.

articles.headline: Week 1, Game by Game
articles.dek: A Monday-night heist, a man who needed seventeen points from one receiver, and the best score in the league losing anyway. Every game in full, plus the board that moved underneath them.

blocks.text: The first week of a fantasy season is mostly noise pretending to be information, and this one was louder than most. The three highest-scoring teams all won and the three lowest all lost, which sounds tidy until you look at moseslin, who scored 161.86 — more than three of the six winners managed — and is 0-1 for his trouble. Two games were still alive on Monday night. One of them turned completely. Here is all of it, and then what it did to the season.

What sizzlemc2 got from two players on Monday night, having gone into it 28.56 points behind a manager whose week was already over. It is the largest single-night swing of the round and the only result that actually changed hands after Sunday.
Four Men Past Twenty, Twice

Domo112 187.06, moseslin 161.86. The best game of the week and the cruellest result in it. Caleb Williams gave Domo112 37.26, the single best performance anywhere on the slate, and Jalen Coker added 35.8. Jahmyr Gibbs — acquired from chassinator in the off-season for Christian McCaffrey — went for 32.1 on his first Sunday in the shirt. Bijan Robinson made it four starters past 27.

moseslin matched him at the top and lost anyway. Christian Watson 34.7, Justin Jefferson 31.2, Lamar Jackson 24.96, Nico Collins 21.2 — four men past twenty of his own. The difference was where the two lineups stopped. Domo112's fifth-best starter scored 16.9; moseslin's scored 14.1, and then it fell away fast: Saquon Barkley 8.5, Rico Dowdle 3.1, a tight end on 4.1.

Domo112 won this with a zero in his lineup — Colston Loveland did nothing at all and it did not matter, which tells you how wide the margin for error was in a game that produced 348.92 points. moseslin has the harder lesson: he is 0-1 with the fourth-highest score in the league, and that is not a problem he can fix by playing better.
Six Ways to Win a Week

jadencha 195.9, drewkim 125.1. The week's high score and its widest margin, and the interesting thing is how ordinary it looked up close. jadencha's best player was D'Andre Swift at 32.9 — only the seventh-best individual score of the round. What he had was six starters between 23 and 33: Swift, Amon-Ra St. Brown 28.7, Jaxon Smith-Njigba 28.2, Isaiah Likely 27.8, Jaxson Dart 26.6, Jonathan Taylor 23.6.

Nothing spectacular, everything good, all at once — and 54 more points on a bench he never needed. Six good scores are much harder to fluke than one enormous one, which is why this is the most convincing performance of the week even though it contains none of its best players.

drewkim's 125.1 was not the disaster the margin implies. Brock Purdy led him with 22.1 and his kicker and defence combined for 35. Seven of his ten starters landed between 6.8 and 14.4 — a floor, not a failure. He ran into the highest score in the league in week one, which is nobody's fault, and left 35.56 on the bench, which is.
Kenneth Walker Stays Up Late

sizzlemc2 162.66, chassinator 144.52. chassinator's week finished on Sunday evening with 144.52 on the board and every starter done. sizzlemc2 was on 115.96 with two men to come. He needed 28.56 from Kenneth Walker and Travis Kelce on Monday night. He got 46.7 — Walker 35.6, Kelce 11.1 — and the game went the other way while chassinator watched.

It was set up by a backfield that did nothing but produce. David Montgomery 27.4 and Javonte Williams 21.7 had already landed on Sunday; with Walker that is 84.7 from three running backs, more than half sizzlemc2's total. Behind them the lineup was thin — Justin Herbert 14.26, Josh Downs 5.7 — and it did not need to be anything else.

chassinator will feel this one for a while. He matched the top end — Ashton Jeanty 30.7, Zay Flowers 29 — and lost at the bottom, where Terry McLaurin managed 3.4 and Cameron Dicker 2, two starting spots producing 5.4 between them. He also left 44.9 on his bench. And it gets worse: Flowers is out for week 2, a 9.0% hit to his expected scoring and the largest availability cost anyone in the league is carrying.
Josh Allen's 35.66 Was Not Enough

saucebossandrew 137.52, jskule23 124.76. Twelve and three-quarter points, the tightest game of the week, and the losing manager had the best player on the field. Josh Allen scored 35.66 and finished as the highest-scoring player on any losing side all week. Nobody else in that lineup reached 23.

It was also alive overnight, if only just. jskule23 finished on Sunday; saucebossandrew went into Monday ahead by 2.86 with Rashee Rice still to play. Rice scored 9.9 and made it comfortable, but a 2.86-point cushion with one man left is not a night anyone enjoys.

saucebossandrew won it the unglamorous way: Chris Olave 30.2, Jalen Hurts 24.72, Breece Hall 19.8, a defence worth 13, and a floor that never gave way — six of ten starters between 7 and 11. He left just 18.2 on the bench, the most efficient lineup of the week by a distance. jskule23 left 43.6 and started a defence that scored nothing. In a game settled by 12.76, either of those is the result.
Fifty Points from Two Roster Spots

wesley55 111.46, victorthompson 90.5. Derrick Henry scored 35.8 and the Pittsburgh defence added 20 — fifty of wesley55's total from two roster spots in a week where nothing else moved. Joe Burrow managed 15.16, then nobody cleared 8.9, and Kyle Pitts finished on zero.

It did not cost him, because victorthompson posted the lowest score in the league. Ladd McConkey 19.2 and Dalton Kincaid 19 were the only real contributions; A.J. Brown managed 5.6, the kicker scored 1 and the defence scored 0. Two roster spots producing a single point between them is how a bad week becomes a 90.5.
And the one man who did produce is now in doubt: McConkey is questionable for week 2. victorthompson's playoff price has already moved further against him than anyone's but bertalicious.
Seventeen Points from Courtland Sutton

bradyrife 105.2, bertalicious 90.74. The lowest-scoring game of the week and the last one to be decided. bradyrife finished on Sunday with 105.2 — Trevor Lawrence 26.1, Chase Brown 16.3, a kicker on 14, and Christian McCaffrey, acquired in the off-season, contributing 11.3 before being traded away again.
bertalicious went into Monday night on 87.64, needing 17.56 from Courtland Sutton to win it. Sutton scored 3.1.

That it came to that at all was the problem. Trey McBride did his job at 24.5 and Bucky Irving added 16.8, but Ja'Marr Chase managed 3.2, the kicker 1 and the defence 1 — four starting spots producing 8.4 points between them. And 53.64 sat on his bench, more than half his own starting total again and nearly four times the margin. bertalicious opened the season at 14.9% to win the whole thing, behind only jadencha and Domo112, and has given back more ground than anyone.
Where the Standings Lie

The site keeps its own ranking, and it does not care who you played. Forty per cent of it is beat-everyone rate — how your score would have fared against all eleven other teams that week rather than the one you drew. Twenty-five per cent is recent form, twenty per cent is points scored, and only fifteen per cent is your actual record. After one week that produces a board which disagrees with the standings in three places.

moseslin sits fourth at 0-1, above three managers who won. chassinator is sixth, also at 0-1, above two more. And bradyrife is tenth despite winning — the lowest-ranked team in the league with a victory, because 105.2 is the third-lowest score anyone posted, and he beat one of the only two teams in the league he would have beaten at all.

This is the whole argument for keeping a board at all. Three of the six games in week 1 were decided by the schedule as much as by the football: moseslin's 161.86 beats three of the six winning scores, and drewkim's 125.1 would have won two of the other games outright. Records reward you for who you were pointed at. This does not.
No arrows yet — this is the first board of the season and there is nothing behind it to move from. From week 2 the movement column starts, and it will be a better read than the ranking itself.
What One Week Did to the Season

The odds board reprices off results, and week 1 moved it more than a single week usually can — partly because there are only fourteen of them, and partly because two of the six were emphatic. These are the changes in each manager's chance of making the playoffs since the draft-day line.

blocks.title: Playoff odds, draft day to now
blocks.sub: Change in each manager's chance of making the six, after one week

blocks.text: sizzlemc2 gained most — sixteen points of playoff probability, from a coin flip to better than one, and he can thank Monday night for all of it. bertalicious lost most, seventeen, and his title chance fell from 14.9% to 9.3%. victorthompson is not far behind at fourteen. At the top, jadencha is now priced at −19900 to make the playoffs, which is the board's way of saying it has seen enough.
Worth keeping in proportion: one week is one game in fourteen, and the model knows it. Nobody's season ended on Sunday. But a fortnight of this and the wildcard race has a shape.
The Matchup: bertalicious v saucebossandrew

Of the six games on the week 2 slate this is the only one the model cannot separate. Their projected win totals are 7.2 and 7.5 — a quarter of a win apart across a whole season — and their playoff odds sit at 57% and 60%. Every other game has a gap of at least 1.4 projected wins.

It is also the week's best story. bertalicious fell furthest on Sunday and saucebossandrew rose second-most, and they now play each other three points apart. The loser drops into the congested middle of the board; the winner gets clear of it. For a week 2 game between a 1-0 and an 0-1 team, there is a surprising amount riding on it.

Elsewhere the slate is lopsided. Domo112 at 91% meets drewkim at 20%, and jadencha at 95% meets moseslin — the best 0-1 team in the league by some distance, who deserves better than the draw he has been handed.
Who to Watch

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.sub: sizzlemc2 · 35.6 on Monday night to steal it

items.name: Ja'Marr Chase
items.delta: in the game of the week

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.delta: the one that did not fire

blocks.text: The injuries are the part that actually moves numbers. Flowers being out is the single largest availability hit in the league and it falls on the manager who can least afford it. Coker's status matters less to Domo112's week than it would to anyone else's — at 91% he can absorb it — but 35.8 is a lot to have in doubt.
The Off-Season Trades

All eight trades on record were done before the season started, and one player was at the centre of most of the noise. Christian McCaffrey never played a snap for the manager who drafted him: chassinator sent him to bradyrife with Kyren Williams coming back, then reacquired him from Domo112 in exchange for Jahmyr Gibbs.

Week 1 was not kind to that arithmetic. Gibbs scored 32.1 for Domo112. McCaffrey scored 11.3 for bradyrife. It is one week and it proves nothing, but it is the sort of one week people bring up in December.

Elsewhere jskule23 sent an eighth-round pick to wesley55 for Luther Burden, who contributed 9.5 on debut, and swapped first-round picks with bertalicious. drewkim and sizzlemc2 exchanged three picks each in a straight reshuffle.
Nobody Has Spent Anything Yet

The first waiver run of the season has not processed. Forty-nine moves have gone through so far and all of them were free-agent pickups, so every manager still has his entire FAAB budget intact and untested.

That is the thing to watch this week rather than any of the football. After a round that produced this many zeroes in starting lineups — two defences on nothing, kickers on 1 and 2, Kyle Pitts and Colston Loveland blank — there will be bids. The first manager to break ranks sets the price for everyone else.

Every score is the official Sleeper total under this league's scoring, taken from the week's own data file. Which night a player played is derived from the NFL schedule. Bench figures are the sum of all non-starting players for the week. Playoff and title probabilities, and the prices beside them, are the site's own live board as it stood on the Tuesday after week 1 — they move as the season is played. Injury costs are the model's estimate of what a lineup loses next week, not a forecast of the player.

articles.headline: The Steepest Fall on the Board
articles.dek: bertalicious lost by 14.46 points, the second-closest game of the week. No manager's title odds or playoff odds fell further.

blocks.text: Every manager's price moved after week 1, because a result came in and the model updated on it. Almost all of those moves were what you would expect: win and your number gets better, lose and it gets worse, roughly in proportion to how it happened. bertalicious is the exception. The loss was ordinary. The move was not.
The drop in bertalicious's playoff probability from the preseason line to today — 73.3% down to 53.3%. It is the largest swing, in either direction, of any of the twelve teams in this league.
Not a blowout

bertalicious lost to bradyrife 105.2 to 90.74, a margin of 14.46 points — the second-closest game of week 1, behind only saucebossandrew's 12.76-point win over jskule23. It was the kind of result that happens to a good team on a bad Sunday, not a sign anything is broken.

Compare it to drewkim, who lost by 70.8 — the widest margin of the week, five times bertalicious's — and saw a playoff probability drop of 5.0 points. A quarter of the damage, for a defeat that was not close to competitive.

blocks.title: Playoff probability, preseason line to now
blocks.sub: Percentage-point change for all twelve teams after week 1

blocks.text: Third favorite, entering

bertalicious opened the season at 530 title odds, an implied 14.9% — the third-shortest price in the league, behind only jadencha (230) and Domo112 (360). One result was enough to push that to 1030 and 8.3%. The 6.6-point drop in title probability is, like the playoff number, the largest of any manager's.

Put next to each other, the two numbers say less about either roster than about how much confidence the preseason line was carrying on one team. A price that falls by four times as much on a competitive loss as another team's falls on a blowout was never really pricing the game — it was pricing an assumption about bertalicious that the game gave the model a reason to unwind all at once.

bertalicious is already back in action, trailing saucebossandrew 5.3 to 17.2 with the model giving the game a 63.2% chance of going the same way. A second loss would not be a blowout either. On this evidence, it would not need to be.

All prices and probabilities from the site's own odds board, comparing the preseason line to the numbers as of week 2. Nothing here is a rank or a projection of where anyone will finish — only how far the board has already moved.

articles.headline: One Game Was on the Bench
articles.dek: The league left 482.22 points in its bench slots. Exactly one of the six losses could have been reversed from there.

blocks.text: Every Tuesday somebody adds up what his bench scored and concludes the week was taken from him. Week 2 hands that argument more ammunition than most: 482.22 points sat in bench slots across the twelve rosters, against 1401.7 actually scored. It is a large number and it is mostly noise. Of the six managers who lost, one could have won by changing a single name.
The points sizzlemc2 left on his bench, more than any other manager in week 2. He lost the game by 18.28.
Kelce for Goedert

sizzlemc2 started Dallas Goedert at tight end and got 1.4 out of him. Travis Kelce was on his bench and scored 25.1. Both are tight ends, so the swap needed no other change, and it is worth 23.7 points against a margin of 18.28 — victorthompson 129.26, sizzlemc2 110.98. Goedert had been added that week, dropping Rashid Shaheed, and went into Sunday carrying a knee sprain and a questionable tag.

The rest of that roster did its job. CeeDee Lamb's 35.3 was the best score on either side of the game, better than anything victorthompson started, and Kenneth Walker added 21.8. It was a winning team with one slot left unattended.
Not close enough to matter

Nobody else was within reach. saucebossandrew came nearest — Xavier Worthy's 13.5 for Michael Wilson's 3.8 is 9.7 points and he lost by 11.62, which leaves him 1.92 short. chassinator had 55.2 sitting there and needed 33.96; Tre Tucker's 25.9 for Rhamondre Stevenson's 3.1 gets him 22.8 of it. Domo112 needed 27.32 and his best bench score was 13.3. jskule23 had 10.1 on his bench, less than anyone in the league, and lost by 23.14. moseslin lost by 66.8, a margin larger than ten of the twelve bench totals in the league.

blocks.title: One swap, six losses
blocks.sub: best bench player in for the worst starter, measured against the margin

blocks.text: Which is the useful way to read a bench total. It measures the scoring a roster had available, not the scoring a manager threw away.
Points left on the bench by the six managers who won, against 227.16 by the six who lost. The winners wasted more of it.

drewkim won by 27.32 with 67.88 unused and Brock Purdy's 28.48 among it. jadencha won by 66.8 with 47.3 left over. A bench full of points is what depth looks like in a week when the starters were already enough, and there is no version of either result where the bench was the story.
The Week in Full
Six games, 120 starters and 1401.7 points — 235.6 fewer than the opening week. One blowout, one game inside twelve points, and four in between. In order of how close they finished.
Eleven Points, and the Best Losing Score of the Week

bertalicious 131.78, saucebossandrew 120.16. The tightest game on the slate and the heaviest — 251.94 between them, separated by 11.62. Ja'Marr Chase went for 26.5 and Stefon Diggs 21.7, and Trey McBride added 18.1 from the tight end slot, which is where most of this league's games were decided.

The move that paid was made on the wire: bertalicious dropped Jared Goff for Baker Mayfield, who returned 13.18 in his first week on the roster. saucebossandrew's 120.16 was the best score any loser posted in week 2 and would have beaten two of the six winners. Chris Olave 22.6, Jalen Hurts 18.16, Sam LaPorta 17.2 — no failure anywhere, just 44.5 more sitting on the bench and 11.62 short.
Allen and Adams Both Cleared Forty

bradyrife 134.06, jskule23 110.92. Josh Allen scored 40.82 and Davante Adams 40.5 — the second and third best individual scores of the week — and they were on opposite sides of the same game. The difference was everything behind them.

bradyrife had Christian McCaffrey at 20.6 and George Kittle at 19; nobody in the jskule23 lineup besides Allen cleared 14. jskule23 also left 10.1 on his bench, less than any manager in the league, which is the honest version of this result: there was no better team available to him. Jayden Reed gave bradyrife 1.4 and it did not matter.
Carolina Outscored Most of a Lineup

wesley55 138.58, chassinator 104.62. The Carolina Panthers put up 27, the best defensive score of the week and the best score in the wesley55 lineup — a week after he added the unit and dropped Pittsburgh for it. Jaylen Waddle 22.8, James Cook 21.4, Derrick Henry 16.2 behind it.

chassinator got 20.3 from Jake Ferguson, himself a free-agent pickup that week, and 16.8 from Parker Washington. He also started Rhamondre Stevenson for 3.1 and Cameron Dicker for 1, and left 55.2 on the bench with Tre Tucker's 25.9 in it. He is 0-2 having scored 249.14, which is more than two of the three unbeaten teams.
Seven Moves, and Mahomes Cut Loose

victorthompson 129.26, sizzlemc2 110.98. Seven roster moves in a week, and the two that mattered both started: Dak Prescott for 29.76 and Devaughn Vele, claimed for $6, for 11.4. The New England Patriots added 23, second only to Carolina among defences. Dalton Kincaid went for 22.5.

The cost was Patrick Mahomes, released to make the Vele claim. It did not hurt — Prescott was already the starter — but it is the kind of move that only looks fine while the starter stays healthy. sizzlemc2 lost this in the tight end slot, which the top of this piece covers: CeeDee Lamb's 35.3 was the best score in the game and it was not enough.
jadencha Has Still Not Been Tested

jadencha 145.1, moseslin 78.3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 44.5, the best individual score anywhere in week 2, and Amon-Ra St. Brown added 35.2. Between them that is 79.7 — more than moseslin's entire lineup managed. Jonathan Taylor's 27.2 made it a formality.

moseslin's 78.3 was the lowest score of the week and it came with Lamar Jackson, Justin Jefferson and Saquon Barkley in the lineup; Barkley returned 2.5 and Jefferson 8.5. jadencha has now won by 70.8 and 66.8 and has scored 341.0, which is 87.75 more than the league average and 67.36 clear of anybody else. He has not played a close game yet.
Domo112 Lost a Hundred Points off His Own Pace

drewkim 112.64, Domo112 85.32. Domo112 scored 187.06 in the opening week, the second-best score in the league. He followed it with 85.32 — a fall of 101.74, the steepest week-to-week swing in either direction this season, and the second-lowest score of week 2.

It was a failure of the whole lineup rather than one slot: Malik Nabers 1.1, Colston Loveland 1.3, Bijan Robinson 9.6, Caleb Williams 8.72. Only Jahmyr Gibbs at 20.3 did anything. drewkim needed very little — DeVonta Smith 27.7 and Omarion Hampton 16.5 — and still left 67.88 unused, Brock Purdy's 28.48 among it. Both teams are 1-1.
Where the Standings Lie

The site keeps its own ranking and it does not care who you played. 40% of it is beat-everyone rate — how you would have done against all eleven other lineups each week rather than the one you drew — 25% the same arithmetic over the last 3 weeks, 20% scoring and only 15% the actual record. After two weeks that produces a board the results table would not recognise.

Two lines in it are worth arguing about. sizzlemc2 is 1-1 and sits above bradyrife, who is 2-0 — because sizzlemc2 has scored 34.38 more and would have beaten more of the league on a neutral schedule. chassinator is 0-2 and sits above victorthompson at 1-1 on the same logic, having outscored him by 29.38.

The movement is where week 2 really landed. moseslin fell 7 places, the steepest drop on the board, after following 161.86 with the lowest score of the week. bradyrife climbed 6 and wesley55 5, which is what back-to-back wins buys when the scoring backs them up. jadencha has not moved, because there is nowhere above him to go.
Two Weeks In, and the Record Does Not Explain It

Three teams are 2-0 — jadencha, wesley55, bradyrife — and three are 0-2: chassinator, moseslin, jskule23. The other six are level. Scoring does not line up behind any of that. sizzlemc2 is 1-1 on 273.64, more than two of the three unbeaten teams. moseslin is 0-2 on 240.16, which is 0.90 more than bradyrife has scored while winning both of his.

blocks.title: Points for, against the league average
blocks.sub: 3039.0 scored across twelve teams · average 253.25 · green 2-0, grey 1-1, red 0-2

blocks.text: Which is the argument for not reading much into two weeks of records. Four of the six teams with a losing record have outscored a team above them, and the schedule is the only reason. That will even out; it has fourteen weeks to.
What Two Weeks Did to the Season

The odds board reprices off results, and two weeks moved it further than the first week alone did. bradyrife gained most — 18.4 points of playoff probability, 42% → 60% — and chassinator gave up 15.3, 39% → 24%. Six of the twelve make the playoffs and 72 games are still to play.

blocks.title: Playoff odds, draft day to now
blocks.sub: two finished weeks priced in · 72 games still to come

blocks.text: Worth keeping in proportion. Two weeks is two games in fourteen and the model treats them that way: nobody is in and nobody is out. jadencha at 97% is the closest thing to settled, and jskule23 at 18% is the furthest from it, having scored 235.68 — more than bertalicious, who is 1-1.

The board on this page counts both finished weeks. Sleeper had not yet moved its season week past 2 when this was written, so it had not posted week 2 into team records either — the site's own board catches up the moment it does, on Tuesday morning. Every game in week 2 was final before a word of this was written.
The Matchup: jadencha v Domo112

The heaviest pairing on the week 3 slate by a distance: 613.38 points between them, against 523.68 for the next one along. It is the unbeaten team with the most points in the league against the team that owns both the second-best single week and the worst collapse of the season.

Elsewhere the slate pairs off exactly. All three unbeaten teams draw a 1-1 opponent and so do all three winless ones: no 2-0 meets a 2-0 and no 0-2 meets a 0-2 anywhere on the board. chassinator gets victorthompson, moseslin gets drewkim, jskule23 gets bertalicious — and that last one is the lightest pairing of the six on combined points at 458.20. bradyrife, 2-0 on less scoring than either of the other unbeaten teams, draws saucebossandrew, who has outscored him by 18.42 while going 1-1.
Eight Dollars, and Nobody Traded

Week 1 produced eight trades. Week 2 produced none at all. Every one of the 22 roster moves came off waivers or the free-agent pool, and only three cost anything: victorthompson $6 for Devaughn Vele, jskule23 $1 for Makai Lemon, victorthompson $1 for Jalen Nailor. Eight dollars, league-wide, in a week.

The claims that will matter are the quiet ones. chassinator took Jake Ferguson off the free-agent pool and got 20.3 out of him immediately. sizzlemc2 added Dallas Goedert, dropping Rashid Shaheed, and started him over Kelce — the single decision that cost a game this week. bradyrife has still committed more budget than anyone this season at $36, all of it in week 1.
Who Is Missing, and What It Costs

7 of the twelve rosters carry at least one starter with a status going into week 3, and the board prices every one of them. The bill runs from 9.9% of a team's week down to 0.1%, which is the difference between a problem and a footnote.

items.sub: Jayden Daniels out (elbow, dislocated) · Alec Pierce out (heel) · Jadarian Price questionable (chest)

items.name: Domo112
items.sub: Caleb Williams out (hamstring, strain) · Mike Evans questionable (hip) · Malik Nabers questionable (shoulder)

items.name: jadencha
items.sub: Jaxson Dart out (knee, sprain) · DJ Moore out (shoulder, sprain)

items.name: moseslin
items.sub: Rico Dowdle out (toe) · Saquon Barkley questionable (arm, stinger)

blocks.text: drewkim carries the heaviest of it at 9.9%, with Jayden Daniels out on a dislocated elbow and Alec Pierce out with a heel. Domo112 is 9.1% lighter with Caleb Williams out and both Malik Nabers and Mike Evans questionable — which, after losing by 27.32 with Nabers on 1.1, is the same problem twice. jadencha is priced 6.3% down and is still the shortest price on the board.

Longer term, four men on DFFL rosters are not playing again this month: Zach Charbonnet (knee - acl, surgery) to 11 October, Omar Cooper (ankle, sprain) to 18 October, Jordan Mason (thumb, surgery) to 25 October, De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle, surgery) to 22 November. None of them costs a manager anything while he stays out of the lineup, which is the point of checking.

A status costs a team for one week only. A man ruled out takes 45% of his share of the lineup off that week's projection — not all of it, because somebody comes off the bench and scores — and nothing is assumed about the week after. The expected return dates above are reported, not priced: a roster carrying a man out until 22 November is charged for next Sunday and no further.

Bench totals cover every non-starting slot. The single-swap test puts each manager's best bench score in place of the worst starter the week file records for him, and only the sizzlemc2 case was checked for position eligibility — the rest are an upper bound on what one change could have done, not a lineup anyone could have set. Points-for and records here are summed from the two weeks' game logs rather than read off Sleeper's standings, which still read one week when this was written. Every score is the official Sleeper total under this league's scoring.

articles.headline: The Fifty-One Dollar Quarterback
articles.dek: jskule23 is 0-2 and has now spent $62 in FAAB this season, more than any other manager in the league. Fifty-one of it went on Patrick Mahomes in a single claim — by itself more than every other manager's full-season total.
articles.standfirst: $51 · the round's only claim in that neighborhood

blocks.text: The waiver wire's biggest move of the last two weeks was not close. jskule23, winless at 0-2, bid $51 to claim Patrick Mahomes off free agency — the largest single FAAB claim of the season, and bigger by itself than the entire season's spending of every other manager in the league.
What jskule23 paid to claim Patrick Mahomes off waivers. It is the largest single bid of the season, and more than any other manager has spent on waivers all year.
A Rival's Discard

Mahomes did not come from nowhere. In the same waiver run, victorthompson released him to claim Devaughn Vele for $6. jskule23 turned around and paid $51 to bring him aboard, dropping Kenyon Sadiq to make room.
The League's Biggest Spender

It is jskule23's third FAAB story of the season. He spent $10 in the league's first waiver round, $1 more on Makai Lemon this week, and the $51 for Mahomes pushes his season total to $62 — the most of any manager in the league, $24 ahead of second-place chassinator's $38.
